newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends unevenly lower in light trade.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends unevenly lower in light trade.

text.p: Light trading activity continued and CME lumber futures retreated late on local pressure to close mostly lower, traders said.

Lumber had drifted higher early following firmer cash prices, but demand lacked followthrough and prices eased on the local pressure. Rolling of March longs and some new bear spreading also weighed on the nearby, they said.

Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $414 per tbf, up $2 from midweek and $6 higher than last Friday. Sales were moderate with mills optimistic over the spring housing market while buyers were cautious, they said.
Lumber closed $3.40 per tbf lower to $0.60 higher with March off most at $403.40 and May off $0.70 at $389.30 per tbf.
